name: Hermetica USDh
oneLiner: USDh is Hermetica's BTC-backed synthetic dollar on Stacks, kept near $1 by pairing spot BTC long with equal-size short BTC perpetual futures positions on CEXes.
collateral: BTC spot holdings paired with equal short BTC perpetual futures positions on centralized exchanges, creating a delta-neutral synthetic dollar position; BTC margin reserves custodied off-exchange via Copper (Clearloop) and Ceffu (MirrorX) institutional settlement providers, with monthly custodian attestations of assets, liabilities and reserve coverage
pegMechanism: Delta-neutral hedging: BTC spot long + equal BTC short perpetual futures neutralize directional exposure; mint and redeem via KYC-gated Hermetica app; DIA oracle provides reserve-backed fair value pricing on Stacks

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved from Pharos stablecoin metadata by the blacklistability resolver; no separate manual override source is attached.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Inferred review retained: USDh resolves to Yes because existing metadata classifies the asset as centralized and no manual override narrows that status.

reserves.name: BTC spot + short BTC perpetual futures (delta-neutral)

mintAuthority.summary: USDh mints only after a two-step backend attestation: a KYC-whitelisted minter calls request-mint and deposits BTC, then Hermetica's trader opens the delta-neutral hedge off-chain and calls confirm-mint to release USDh, making supply gated by Hermetica's off-chain operator.

controls.label: Hermetica trader / minting backend (confirm-mint)
controls.evidence: Hermetica Stacks minting contract uses a request-mint to confirm-mint flow: a whitelisted minter deposits BTC, then a Hermetica-operated trader opens the off-chain perpetual hedge and calls confirm-mint to mint USDh; no permissionless on-chain mint exists.

controls.label: Minter whitelist (KYC/KYB gate)
controls.evidence: Only KYC/KYB-approved participants whitelisted by Hermetica can request mints/redemptions directly; access to the mint route is administered off-chain by the issuer.

review.evidence: Hermetica's technical docs describe a backend-attested mint: request-mint deposits BTC, an off-chain trader establishes the BTC short hedge, and confirm-mint then issues USDh; redemption mirrors this via confirm-redeem. Mint is gated by both whitelisting and the issuer's off-chain confirmation, consistent with an offchain-attested-minter under a concentrated operator.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the on-chain Stacks principal(s) authorized as trader/whitelist admin and any upgrade authority on the usdh-token-v1 contract before raising confidence.
